body.statement: Let a nonempty semialgebraic set in \(\mathbb R^k\) be specified by a first-order formula whose integer input polynomials have total encoding length \(\Lambda_0\), number at most \(s\), and degree at most \(D\).  Real quantifier elimination and sample-point construction return a point whose coordinates are real algebraic numbers, each represented by a square-free integer polynomial and a rational isolating interval, within \((\Lambda_0sD)^{2^{O(k)}}\) bit operations.

source.locator: Renegar, On the Computational Complexity and Geometry of the First-Order Theory of the Reals, Part III: Quantifier Elimination, Journal of Symbolic Computation 13 (1992), pp. 329--352; quantifier-elimination complexity and algebraic sample-point output

attestation.note: The stable publisher record was checked.  The deliberately loose double-exponential corollary used here is weaker than Renegar's quantitative bounds and includes exact real-algebraic sample-point representation.
